heading: Delhi High Court shields Nagarjuna’s personality rights, blocks misused content
paragraphs: The Delhi High Court has passed an order protecting the personality and moral rights of Telugu actor Nagarjuna Akkineni by restraining several entities from using his name, image, or other persona attributes exclusively identifiable with him without his consent.

In its interim order, the court specifically restrained websites from violating his personality rights and moral rights and from passing off their goods and services as those emanating from or endorsed by him.
The court observed that it is prima facie clear that the attributes of his persona, including his name and images, are being misused by the defendant websites without any authorisation from him.

The court noted that exploitation of one’s personality rights puts at risk not only economic interests but also the right to live with dignity, potentially causing immeasurable harm to reputation and goodwill. It observed that Nagarjuna is a celebrated personality in the entertainment industry, and any depiction of him in misleading, derogatory, or inappropriate settings will inevitably dilute the goodwill and reputation associated with him.

The court has directed 10 defendant websites, which are alleged to be using Nagarjuna’s name in connection with pornographic content, to take down, remove, disable, or block the relevant URLs within 72 hours of receiving the notice.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Department of Telecommunications, Government of India, have been directed to issue necessary directions to block and disable some URLs within seven days.
The actor’s suit seeks a permanent injunction restraining the misappropriation of personality or publicity rights, infringement of performer’s rights, and passing off.
